title: Testing Whether Safety Alignment Survives Quantization (INT4 vs. FP16)
original_idea: Compare ASR across attack types (prefilling, direct harmful prompts, GCG) between FP16 and INT4 (GGUF/GPTQ) versions of the same model. Use Llama-3-8B as the test model. Measure ASR on 30 harmful prompts and compare first-token refusal probabilities.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The quantization-safety interaction has been characterized with nuanced findings (non-monotonic effects, different results for direct vs. transfer attacks). The proposed experiment would not add new theoretical insight.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running GCG attacks and extracting first-token probabilities, which demands some ML experience. Quantization tooling (llama.cpp, GPTQ) is well-documented. GCG is harder for beginners. Medium compute covers Llama-3-8B.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single model, two quantization levels, 30 prompts. Clear comparison. GCG adds complexity but the deliverable is focused.

novelty.reasoning: This is directly addressed by multiple 2025 papers. 'On Jailbreaking Quantized Language Models Through Fault Injection Attacks' (GLSVLSI 2025) tests Llama-3-8B across FP16, FP8, INT8, and INT4, finding FP16 models have >80% ASR while INT4 shows different robustness profiles. 'Q-ReSafe: Assessing Safety Risks and Quantization-aware Safety Patching for Quantized LLMs' (OpenReview 2025) directly assesses safety risks under quantization. 'Preserving Fairness and Safety in Quantized LLMs Through Critical Weight Protection' (arXiv:2601.12033, 2026) proposes mitigations. The proposed experiment (compare ASR across FP16 and INT4 on Llama-3-8B) is a strict subset of published work.
